policy.introduction: Subnational executive governance across Nigeria recorded an active composite Policy Signal Index (PSI) baseline average of 8.3 on November 12, 2026, across 19 active jurisdictions. State executives prioritized massive capital budget proposals, judicial and legislative welfare reforms, public utility rehabilitations, and large-scale agricultural commercialization.

Furthermore, legislative and judicial reforms gained strong traction, evidenced by Abia State becoming the first South-East state to approve 25% CONLESS for parliamentary staff and Ogun State allocating 49 duplexes to High Court judges.
policy.strategicOutlook: Sustaining momentum requires fast-tracking legislative review of the 2027 appropriation bills, ensuring rapid execution of ward-level solar water projects, and maintaining strict compliance with host-community provisions in energy and mining sectors.
policy.conclusion: The subnational executive landscape reflects exceptional commitment to fiscal expansion, structural governance reforms, rural utility deployment, and public institutional welfare.

security.strategicOutlook: Private capital and international partners can operate with increased confidence in jurisdictions demonstrating strict adherence to executive oversight, judicial independence, and rule of law enforcement.
security.conclusion: Proactive executive interventions, public security partnerships, and institutional rights protections continue to maintain a highly stable environment across economic zones.
